key_insight: A humanoid controller can often solve new tasks at test time by reusing and refining skills it already has, rather than being retrained from scratch. The paper shows that an expressive planning-control interface can unlock this latent competence for contact-rich, multi-stage loco-manipulation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to make humanoid robots perform novel loco-manipulation tasks they were never explicitly trained for, while improving through their own attempts and retaining learned behavior without retraining.
method: Use test-time evolution to adapt reward programs based on task performance during rollout.
Repurpose an existing broad controller by linking high-level planning with low-level control through an expressive interface.
Iteratively improve behavior from the robot's own attempts, enabling skill reuse and retention instead of offline retraining.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical path for deploying humanoid robots in new, real-world tasks with less data and less retraining. For AI/ML practitioners, it suggests a scalable way to extend capabilities at inference time by evolving reward specifications rather than rebuilding policies.

paper_title: InterEvolve: Test-Time Evolution of Reward Programs for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
paper_authors: Zhuo Lin, Sirui Xu, Liuyu Bian, Yu-Xiong Wang, Liang-Yan Gui
